brewer: One who brews; one whose occupation is to prepare malt liquors.

branchiura: A group of Entomostraca, with suctorial mouths, including species parasitic on fishes, as the carp lice (Argulus).
bromide: A compound of bromine with a positive radical.
breastplate: 1. A plate of metal covering the breast as defensive armor. Before his old rusty breastplate could be scoured, and his cracked headpiece mended. Swift. 2. A piece against which the workman presses his breast in operating a breast drill, or other similar tool. 3. A strap that runs across a horse's breast. Ash. 4.
bronchopneumonia: Inflammation of the bronchi and lungs; catarrhal pneumonia.
brownie: An imaginary good-natured spirit, who was supposed often to perform important services around the house by night, such as thrashing, churning, sweeping. [Scot.]
bronze: 1. An alloy of copper and tin, to which small proportions of other metals, especially zinc, are sometimes added. It is hard and sonorous, and is used for statues, bells, cannon, etc., the proportions… | 1. To give an appearance of bronze to, by a coating of bronze powder, or by other means; to make of the color of bronze; as, to bronze plaster casts; to bronze coins or medals.
brog: A pointed instrument, as a joiner's awl, a brad awl, a needle, or a small ship stick. | To prod with a pointed instrument, as a lance; also, to broggle. [Scot. & Prov.] Sir W. Scott.
breastbeam: The front transverse beam of a locomotive.
britt: (a) The young of the common herring; also, a small species of herring; the sprat. (b) The minute marine animals (chiefly Entomostraca) upon which the right whales feed.
branching: Furnished with branches; shooting our branches; extending in a branch or branches. Shaded with branching palm. Milton. | The act or state of separation into branches; division into branches; a division or branch. The sciences, with their numerous branchings. L. Watts.
brame: Sharp passion; vexation. (old) Heart-burning brame. Spenser.
broadcloth: A fine smooth-faced woolen cloth for men's garments, usually of double width (i.e., a yard and a half); -- so called in distinction from woolens three quarters of a yard wide.
bryology: That part of botany which relates to mosses.
broadside: 1. (Naut.) The side of a ship above the water line, from the bow to the quarter. 2. A discharge of or from all the guns on one side of a ship, at the same time. 3. A volley of abuse or denunciation. [Colloq.] 4. (Print.) A sheet of paper containing one large page, or printed on one side only; -- called also broadsheet.
brusher: One who, or that which, brushes.
brevet: 1. A warrant from the government, granting a privilege, title, or dignity. [French usage]. 2. (Mil.) A commission giving an officer higher rank than that for which he receives pay; | To confer rank upon by brevet.
bronzewing: An Australian pigeon of the genus Phaps, of several species; -- so called from its bronze plumage.
bristletail: An insect of the genera Lepisma, Campodea, etc., belonging to the Thysanura.
brelancarre: In French games, a double pair royal.
brainy: Having an active or vigorous mind. [Colloq.]
brewage: Malt liquor; drink brewed. "Some well-spiced brewage." Milton. A rich brewage, made of the best Spanish wine. Macaulay.
brickmaker: One whose occupation is to make bricks. -- Brick"mak*ing, n.
brushturkey: A large, edible, gregarious bird of Australia (Talegalla Lathami) of the family Megapodidæ. Also applied to several allied species of New Guinea. Note: The brush turkeys live in the "brush," and construct a common nest by collecting a large heap of decaying vegetable matter, which generates heat sufficient to hatch the numerous eggs (sometimes half a bushel) deposited in it by…
brockenspectre: A mountain specter (which see), esp. that observed on the Brocken, in the Harz Mountains.
bridgeboard: 1. (Arch.) A notched board to which the treads and risers of the steps of wooden stairs are fastened. 2. A board or plank used as a bridge.
breed: 1. To produce as offspring; to bring forth; to bear; to procreate; to generate; to beget; to hatch. Yet every mother breeds not sons alike. Shak. If the sun breed maggots in a dead dog. Shak. 2. | 1. To bear and nourish young; to reproduce or multiply itself; to be pregnant. That they breed abundantly in the earth. Gen. viii. 17. The mother had never bred before. Carpenter. Ant.
bromeliaceous: Pertaining to, or resembling, a family of endogenous and mostly epiphytic or saxicolous plants of which the genera Tillandsia and Billbergia are examples. The pineapple, though terrestrial, is also of this family.
brushing: 1. Constructed or used to brush with; as a brushing machine. 2. Brisk; light; as, a brushing gallop.
brast: To burst. (old) And both his yën braste out of his face. Chaucer. Dreadfull furies which their chains have brast. Spenser.
branchy: Full of branches; having wide-spreading branches; consisting of branches. Beneath thy branchy bowers of thickest gloom. J. Scott.
brickbat: A piece or fragment of a brick. See Bat, 4. Bacon.
breviloquence: A brief and pertinent mode of speaking.
brother: 1. A male person who has the same father and mother with another person, or who has one of them only. In the latter case he is more definitely called a half brother, or brother of the half blood. | To make a brother of; to call or treat as a brother; to admit to a brotherhood. Sir W. Scott.
broncho: A native or a Mexican horse of small size. [Western U.S.]
brahmin: A person of the highest or sacerdotal caste among the Hindoos. Brahman bull (Zoöl.), the male of a variety of the zebu, or Indian ox, considered sacred by the Hindoos.
broadgauge: A wider distance between the rails than the "standard" gauge of four feet eight inches and a half. See Gauge.
brin: One of the radiating sticks of a fan. The outermost are larger and longer, and are called panaches. Knight.
bromegrass: A genus (Bromus) of grasses, one species of which is the chess or cheat.
braille: A system of printing or writing for the blind in which the characters are represented by tangible points or dots. It was invented by Louis Braille, a French teacher of the blind.
brusqueness: Quality of being brusque; roughness joined with promptness; blutness. Brit. Quar.
brigandish: Like a brigand or freebooter; robberlike.
brills: The hair on the eyelids of a horse. Bailey.
broadbill: 1. (Zoöl.) A wild duck (Aythya, or Fuligula, marila), which appears in large numbers on the eastern coast of the United States, in autumn; - - called also bluebill, blackhead, raft duck, and scaup duck. See Scaup duck. 2. (Zoöl.) The shoveler. See Shoveler.
brock: A badger. Or with pretense of chasing thence the brock. B. Jonson.
browbeat: To depress or bear down with haughty, stern looks, or with arrogant speech and dogmatic assertions; to abash or disconcert by impudent or abusive words or looks; to bully; as, to browbeat witnesses. My grandfather was not a man to be browbeaten. W. Irving.
brandenburg: A kind of decoration for the breast of a coat, sometimes only a frog with a loop, but in some military uniforms enlarged into a broad horizontal stripe. He wore a coat . . . trimmed with Brandenburgs. Smollett.
brigandine: A coast of armor for the body, consisting of scales or plates, sometimes overlapping each other, generally of metal, and sewed to linen or other material. It was worn in the Middle Ages. [Written also brigantine.] Jer. xlvi. 4. Then put on all thy gorgeous arms, thy helmet, And brigandine of brass. Milton.
branchia: A gill; a respiratory organ for breathing the air contained in water, such as many aquatic and semiaquatic animals have.
brattice: (a) A wall of separation in a shaft or gallery used for ventilation. (b) Planking to support a roof or wall.
briquette: 1. A block of compacted coal dust, or peat, etc., for fuel. 2. A block of artificial stone in the form of a brick, used for paving; also, a molded sample of solidified cement or mortar for use as a test piece for showing the strength of the material.
browspot: A rounded organ between the eyes of the frog; the interocular gland.
brownian: Pertaining to Dr. Robert Brown, who first demonstrated (about 1827) the commonness of the motion described below. Brownian movement, the peculiar, rapid, vibratory movement exhibited by the microscopic particles of substances when suspended in water or other fluids.
bryozoum: An individual zooid of a bryozoan coralline, of which there may be two or more kinds in a single colony. The zooecia usually have a wreath of tentacles around the mouth, and a well developed stomach and intestinal canal; but these parts are lacking in the other zooids (Avicularia, Ooecia, etc.).
broadleaved: Having broad, or relatively broad, leaves. Keats.
breather: 1. One who breathes. Hence: (a) One who lives.(b) One who utters. (c) One who animates or inspires. 2. That which puts one out of breath, as violent exercise. [Colloq.]
brochantite: A basic sulphate of copper, occurring in emerald-green crystals.
brahma: 1. (Hindoo Myth.) The One First Cause; also, one of the triad of Hindoo gods. The triad consists of Brahma, the Creator, Vishnu, the Preserver, and Siva, the Destroyer.
broaden: To grow broad; to become broader or wider. The broadening sun appears. Wordsworth. | To make broad or broader; to render more broad or comprehensive.
browsewood: Srubs and bushes upon which animals browse.
bring: 1. To convey to the place where the speaker is or is to be; to bear from a more distant to a nearer place; to fetch. And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread. 1 Kings xvii. 11. To France shall we convey you safe, And bring you back. Shak. 2. To cause the accession or obtaining of; to procure; to make to come;
brachiata: A division of the Crinoidea, including those furnished with long jointed arms. See Crinoidea.
breakaway: 1. A wild rush of sheep, cattle, horses, or camels (especially at the smell or the sight of water); a stampede. 2. An animal that breaks away from a herd.
brattishing: 1. See Brattice, n. 2. (Arch.) Carved openwork, as of a shrine, battlement, or parapet.
brewis: 1. Broth or pottage. (old) Let them of their Bonner's "beef" and "broth" make what brewis they please for their credulous guests. Bp. Hall. 2. Bread soaked in broth, drippings of roast meat, milk, or water and butter.
briticism: A word, phrase, or idiom peculiar to Great Britain; any manner of using a word or words that is peculiar to Great Britain.
brag: To talk about one's self, or things pertaining to one's self, in a manner intended to excite admiration, envy, or wonder; to talk boastfully; to boast; -- often followed by of; | 1. A boast or boasting; bragging; ostentatious pretense or self glorification. Cæsar . . . made not here his brag Of "came," and "saw," and "overcame." Shak. 2. The thing which is boasted of.
brecciated: Consisting of angular fragments cemented together; resembling breccia in appearance. The brecciated appearance of many specimens [of meteorites]. H. A. Newton.
brainless: Without understanding; silly; thougthless; witless. -- Brain"less*ness, n.
brickkiln: A kiln, or furnace, in which bricks are baked or burnt; or a pile of green bricks, laid loose, with arches underneath to receive the wood or fuel for burning them.
brooch: 1. An ornament, in various forms, with a tongue, pin, or loop for attaching it to a garment; now worn at the breast by women; a breastpin. Formerly worn by men on the hat. Honor 's a good brooch to wear in a man's hat. B. Jonson. 2. (Paint.) A painting all of one color, as a sepia painting, or an India painting.
bromic: Of, pertaining to, or containing, bromine; -- said of those compounds of bromine in which this element has a valence of five, or the next to its highest; as, bromic acid.
breviary: 1. An abridgment; a compend; an epitome; a brief account or summary. A book entitled the abridgment or breviary of those roots that are to be cut up or gathered. Holland. 2.
brutalization: The act or process of making brutal; state of being brutalized.
branchless: Destitude of branches or shoots; without any valuable product; barren; naked.
brillante: In a gay, showy, and sparkling style.
bricky: Full of bricks; formed of bricks; resembling bricks or brick dust. Spenser.
breccia: A rock composed of angular fragments either of the same mineral or of different minerals, etc., united by a cement, and commonly presenting a variety of colors. Bone breccia, a breccia containing bones, usually fragmentary. -- Coin breccia, a breccia containing coins.
brassica: A genus of plants embracing several species ad varieties differing much in appearance and qualities: such as the common cabbage (B. oleracea), broccoli, cauliflowers, etc.; the wild turnip (B. campestris); the common turnip (B. rapa); the rape of coleseed (B. napus), etc.
bright: 1. Radiating or reflecting light; shedding or having much light; shining; luminous; not dark. The sun was bright o'erhead. Longfellow. The earth was dark, but the heavens were bright. Drake. | Splendor; brightness. (poetic) Dark with excessive bright thy skirts appear. Milton.
breadless: Without bread; destitude of food. Plump peers and breadless bards alike are dull. P. Whitehead.
browny: Brown or, somewhat brown. "Browny locks." Shak.
brachiopoda: A class of Molluscoidea having a symmetrical bivalve shell, often attached by a fleshy peduncle. Note: Within the shell is a pair of "arms," often long and spirally coiled, bearing rows of ciliated tentacles by which a current of water is made to flow into the mantle cavity, bringing the microscopic food to the mouth between the bases of the arms.
brandspore: One of several spores growing in a series or chain, and produced by one of the fungi called brand.
braxy: 1. A disease of sheep. The term is variously applied in different localities. [Scot.] 2. A diseased sheep, or its mutton.
brawny: Having large, strong muscles; muscular; fleshy; strong. "Brawny limbs." W. Irving. Syn. -- Muscular; fleshy; strong; bulky; sinewy; athletic; stalwart; powerful; robust.
breastplow: A kind of plow, driven by the breast of the workman; -- used to cut or pare turf.
brasilin: A substance, C16H14O5, extracted from brazilwood as a yellow crystalline powder which is white when pure. It is colored intensely red by alkalies on exposure to the air, being oxidized to bra*sil"e*in, C16H12O5, to which brazilwood owes its dyeing properties.
breechcloth: A cloth worn around the breech.
broke: 1. To transact business for another. Brome. 2. To act as procurer in love matters; to pimp. (old) We do want a certain necessary woman to broke between them, Cupid said. Fanshawe. And brokes with all that can in such a suit Corrupt the tender honor of a maid. Shak.
brained: Supplied with brains. If th' other two be brained like us. Shak.
bract: (a) A leaf, usually smaller than the true leaves of a plant, from the axil of which a flower stalk arises. (b) Any modified leaf, or scale, on a flower stalk or at the base of a flower. Note: Bracts are often inconspicuous, but sometimes large and showy, or highly colored, as in many cactaceous plants. The spathes of aroid plants are conspicuous forms of bracts.
brasque: A paste made by mixing powdered charcoal, coal, or coke with clay, molasses, tar, or other suitable substance. It is used for lining hearths, crucibles, etc. Called also steep.
brimstony: Containing or resembling brimstone; sulphurous. B. Jonson.
bramahpress: A hydrostatic press of immense power, invented by Joseph Bramah of London. See under Hydrostatic.
bromate: To combine or impregnate with bromine; as, bromated camphor.
breastbone: The bone of the breast; the sternum.
brabbler: A clamorous, quarrelsome, noisy fellow; a wrangler. [R] Shak.
bromol: A crystalline substance (chemically, tribromophenol, C6H2Br3OH), used as an antiseptic and disinfectant.
brede: A braid. Half lapped in glowing gauze and golden brede. Tennyson.
branchiomerism: The state of being made up of branchiate segments. R. Wiedersheim.
brisket: That part of the breast of an animal which extends from the fore legs back beneath the ribs; also applied to the fore part of a horse, from the shoulders to the bottom of the chest. Note: [See Illust. of Beef.]
bravely: 1. In a brave manner; courageously; gallantly; valiantly; splendidly; nobly. 2. Finely; gaudily; gayly; showily. And [she] decked herself bravely to allure the eyes of all men that should see her. Judith. x. 4. 3. Well; thrivingly; prosperously. [Colloq.]
bricole: A kind of traces with hooks and rings, with which men drag and maneuver guns where horses can not be used.
bristliness: The quality or state of having bristles.
break: 1. To strain apart; to sever by fracture; to divide with violence; as, to break a rope or chain; to break a seal; to break an axle; to break rocks or coal; to break a lock. Shak. 2. | 1. To come apart or divide into two or more pieces, usually with suddenness and violence; to part; to burst asunder. 2. To open spontaneously, or by pressure from within, as a bubble, a tumor, a seed…
breakneck: 1. A fall that breaks the neck. 2. A steep place endangering the neck. | Producing danger of a broken neck; as, breakneck speed.
brownthrush: A common American singing bird (Harporhynchus rufus), allied to the mocking bird; -- also called brown thrasher.
brininess: The state or quality of being briny; saltness; brinishness.
brumal: Of or pertaining to winter. "The brumal solstice." Sir T. Browne.
bridge: 1. A structure, usually of wood, stone, brick, or iron, erected over a river or other water course, or over a chasm, railroad, etc., to make a passageway from one bank to the other. 2. | 1. To build a bridge or bridges on or over; as, to bridge a river. Their simple engineering bridged with felled trees the streams which could not be forded. Palfrey. 2.
brazenness: The quality or state of being brazen. Johnson.
brown: Of a dark color, of various shades between black and red or yellow. Cheeks brown as the oak leaves. Longfellow. Brown Bess, the old regulation flintlock smoothbore musket, with bronzed barrel,… | A dark color inclining to red or yellow, resulting from the mixture of red and black, or of red, black, and yellow; a tawny, dusky hue.
brahmanism: The religion or system of doctrines of the Brahmans; the religion of Brahma.
breve: 1. (Mus.) A note or character of time, equivalent to two semibreves or four minims. When dotted, it is equal to three semibreves. It was formerly of a square figure (as thus: Moore. 2. (Law) Any writ or precept under seal, issued out of any court. 3. (Print.) A curved mark [˘] used commonly to indicate the short quantity of a vowel. 4.
brachystochrone: A curve, in which a body, starting from a given point, and descending solely by the force of gravity, will reach another given point in a shorter time than it could by any other path. This curve of quickest descent, as it is sometimes called, is, in a vacuum, the same as the cycloid.
breakwater: Any structure or contrivance, as a mole, or a wall at the mouth of a harbor, to break the force of waves, and afford protection from their violence.
brindled: Having dark streaks or spots on a gray or tawny ground; brinded. "With a brindled lion played." Churchill.
brachelytra: A group of beetles having short elytra, as the rove beetles.
brit: (a) The young of the common herring; also, a small species of herring; the sprat. (b) The minute marine animals (chiefly Entomostraca) upon which the right whales feed.
brasilein: A substance, C16H14O5, extracted from brazilwood as a yellow crystalline powder which is white when pure. It is colored intensely red by alkalies on exposure to the air, being oxidized to bra*sil"e*in, C16H12O5, to which brazilwood owes its dyeing properties.
briefless: Having no brief; without clients; as, a briefless barrister.
brehon: An ancient Irish or Scotch judge. Brehon laws, the ancient Irish laws, -- unwritten, like the common law of England. They were abolished by statute of Edward III.
brachium: The upper arm; the segment of the fore limb between the shoulder and the elbow.
brachydome: A dome parallel to the shorter lateral axis. See Dome.
breezefly: A fly of various species, of the family Tabanidæ, noted for buzzing about animals, and tormenting them by sucking their blood; -- called also horsefly, and gadfly. They are among the largest of two- winged or dipterous insects. The name is also given to different species of botflies. [Written also breese and brize.]
brave: 1. Bold; courageous; daring; intrepid; -- opposed to cowardly; as, a brave man; a brave act. 2. Having any sort of superiority or excellence; -- especially such as in conspicuous. [Obs. | 1. A brave person; one who is daring. The star-spangled banner, O,long may it wave O'er the land of the free and the home of the brave. F. S. Key. 2. Specifically, an Indian warrior. 3.
broiler: One who excites broils; one who engages in or promotes noisy quarrels. What doth he but turn broiler, . . . make new libels against the church Hammond. | 1. One who broils, or cooks by broiling. 2. A gridiron or other utensil used in broiling. 3. A chicken or other bird fit for broiling. [Colloq.]
brittle: Easily broken; apt to break; fragile; not tough or tenacious. Farewell, thou pretty, brittle piece Of fine-cut crystal. Cotton. Brittle silver ore, the mineral stephanite.
brassiness: The state, conditions, or quality of being brassy. [Colloq.]
bribery: 1. Robbery; extortion. (old) 2. The act or practice of giving or taking bribes; the act of influencing the official or political action of another by corrupt inducements. Bribery oath, an oath taken by a person that he has not been bribed as to voting. [Eng.]
broadsword: A sword with a broad blade and a cutting edge; a claymore. I heard the broadsword's deadly clang. Sir W. Scott.
bronzite: A variety of enstatite, often having a bronzelike luster. It is a silicate of magnesia and iron, of the pyroxene family.
brotherhood: 1. The state of being brothers or a brother. 2. An association for any purpose, as a society of monks; a fraternity. 3. The whole body of persons engaged in the same business, -- especially those of the same profession; as, the legal or medical brotherhood. 4. Persons, and, poetically, things, of a like kind. A brotherhood of venerable trees. Wordsworth. Syn. -- Fraternity;
bronchitis: Inflammation, acute or chronic, of the bronchial tubes or any part of them.
brandnew: Quite new; bright as if fresh from the forge.
breechaction: The breech mechanism in breech-loading small arms and certain special guns, as automatic and machine guns; --used frequently in referring to the method by which the movable barrels of breech- loading shotguns are locked, unlocked, or rotated to loading position.
broadbrim: 1. A hat with a very broad brim, like those worn by men of the society of Friends. 2. A member of the society of Friends; a Quaker. [Sportive]
brachioganoidei: An order of ganoid fishes of which the bichir of Africa is a living example. See Crossopterygii.
bronchophony: A modification of the voice sounds, by which they are intensified and heightened in pitch; -- observed in auscultation of the chest in certain cases of intro-thoracic disease.
bridgehead: A fortification commanding the extremity of a bridge nearest the enemy, to insure the preservation and usefulness of the bridge, and prevent the enemy from crossing; a tête-de-pont.
bracketing: A series or group of brackets; brackets, collectively.
brawniness: The quality or state of being brawny.
breastwork: 1. (Fort.) A defensive work of moderate height, hastily thrown up, of earth or other material. 2. (Naut.) A railing on the quarter-deck and forecastle.
brotherly: Of or pertaining to brothers; such as is natural for brothers; becoming to brothers; kind; affectionate; as, brotherly love. Syn. -- Fraternal; kind; affectionate; tender. | Like a brother; affectionately; kindly. "I speak but brotherly of him." Shak.
brutely: In a rude or violent manner.
brassicaceous: Related to, or resembling, the cabbage, or plants of the Cabbage family.
brahman: A person of the highest or sacerdotal caste among the Hindoos. Brahman bull (Zoöl.), the male of a variety of the zebu, or Indian ox, considered sacred by the Hindoos.
broomstick: A stick used as a handle of a broom.
bromanil: A substance analogous to chloranil but containing bromine in place of chlorine.
brevity: 1. Shortness of duration; briefness of time; as, the brevity of human life. 2. Contraction into few words; conciseness. Brevity is the soul of wit. Shak. This argument is stated by St. John with his usual elegant brevity and simplicity. Bp. Porteus. Syn. -- Shortness; conciseness; succinctness; terseness.
breath: 1. The air inhaled and exhaled in respiration, air which, in the process of respiration, has parted with oxygen and has received carbonic acid, aqueous vapor, warmth, etc. Melted as breath into the wind. Shak. 2. The act of breathing naturally or freely; the power or capacity to breathe freely; as, I am out of breath. 3. The power of respiration, and hence, life. Hood.
broadcast: A casting or throwing seed in all directions, as from the hand in sowing. | 1. Cast or dispersed in all directions, as seed from the hand in sowing; widely diffused. 2. Scattering in all directions (as a method of sowing); -- opposed to planting in hills, or rows.
bridoon: The snaffle and rein of a military bridle, which acts independently of the bit, at the pleasure of the rider. It is used in connection with a curb bit, which has its own rein. Campbell.
breastfast: A large rope to fasten the midship part of a ship to a wharf, or to another vessel.
brocket: 1. (Zoöl.) A male red deer two years old; -- sometimes called brock. 2. (Zoöl.) A small South American deer, of several species (Coassus superciliaris, C. rufus, and C. auritus).
braiding: 1. The act of making or using braids. 2. Braids, collectively; trimming. A gentleman enveloped in mustachios, whiskers, fur collars, and braiding. Thackeray.
brochette: A small spit or skewer. -- En bro`chette" (än) [F.], on a brochette; skewered.
briskness: Liveliness; vigor in action; quickness; gayety; vivacity; effervescence.
briery: A place where briers grow. Huloet.
brat: 1. A coarse garnment or cloak; also, coarse clothing, in general. (old) Chaucer. 2. A coarse kind of apron for keeping the clothes clean; a bib. [Prov. Eng. & Scot.] Wright. 3. A child; an offspring; | A thin bed of coal mixed with pyrites or carbonate of lime.
breadthwise: In the direction of the breadth.
broggle: To sniggle, or fish with a brog. [Prov. Eng.] Wright.
brig: A two-masted, square-rigged vessel. Hermaphrodite brig, a two- masted vessel square-rigged forward and schooner-rigged aft. See Illustration in Appendix.
brazier: An artificer who works in brass. Franklin. | A pan for holding burning coals.
brimmed: 1. Having a brim; -- usually in composition. "Broad-brimmed hat." Spectator. 2. Full to, or level with, the brim. Milton.
browed: Having (such) a brow; -- used in composition; as, dark-browed, stern-browed.
bromidiom: A conventional comment or saying, such as those characteristic of bromides. [Slang]
breakage: 1. The act of breaking; a break; a breaking; also, articles broken. 2. An allowance or compensation for things broken accidentally, as in transportation or use.
bromalin: A colorless or white crystalline compound, (CH2)6N4C2H5Br, used as a sedative in epilepsy.
brawling: 1. Quarreling; quarrelsome; noisy. She is an irksome brawling scold. Shak. 2. Making a loud confused noise. See Brawl, v. i., 3. A brawling stream. J. S. Shairp.
breathlessness: The state of being breathless or out of breath.
brachyura: A group of decapod Crustacea, including the common crabs, characterized by a small and short abdomen, which is bent up beneath the large cephalo-thorax. [Also spelt Brachyoura.] See Crab, and Illustration in Appendix.
brandy: A strong alcoholic liquor distilled from wine. The name is also given to spirit distilled from other liquors, and in the United States to that distilled from cider and peaches. In northern Europe, it is also applied to a spirit obtained from grain. Brandy fruit, fruit preserved in brandy and sugar.
broiling: Excessively hot; as, a broiling sun. -- n. The act of causing anything to broil.
brake: 1. (Bot.) A fern of the genus Pteris, esp. the P. aquilina, common in almost all countries. It has solitary stems dividing into three principal branches. Less properly: Any fern. 2. A thicket; | 1. An instrument or machine to break or bruise the woody part of flax or hemp so that it may be separated from the fiber. 2. An extended handle by means of which a number of men can unite in working…
brahmanist: An adherent of the religion of the Brahmans.
brigantine: 1. A practical vessel. (old) 2. A two-masted, square-rigged vessel, differing from a brig in that she does not carry a square mainsail. 3. See Brigandine.
broadleaf: A tree (Terminalia latifolia) of Jamaica, the wood of which is used for boards, scantling, shingles, etc; -- sometimes called the almond tree, from the shape of its fruit.
broadseal: To stamp with the broad seal; to make sure; to guarantee or warrant. (old) Thy presence broadseals our delights for pure. B. Jonson.
brike: A breach; ruin; downfall; peril. (old) Chaucer.
brazenface: An impudent of shameless person. "Well said, brazenface; hold it out." Shak.
brahminical: Of or pertaining to the Brahmans or to their doctrines and worship.

brokery: The business of a broker. (old) And with extorting, cozening, forfeiting, And tricks belonging unto brokery. Marlowe.
briefman: 1. One who makes a brief. 2. A copier of a manuscript.
brimstone: Made of, or pertaining to, brimstone; as, brimstone matches. From his brimstone bed at break of day A-walking the devil has gone. Coleridge.

bridgetree: The beam which supports the spindle socket of the runner in a grinding mill. Knight.

brokenwinded: Having short breath or disordered respiration, as a horse.

braiser: A kettle or pan for braising.

brancard: A litter on which a person may be carried. (old) Coigrave.

brigade: 1. (Mil.) A body of troops, whether cavalry, artillery, infantry, or mixed, consisting of two or more regiments, under the command of a brigadier general. Note: Two or more brigades constitute a… | To form into a brigade, or into brigades.
bridgeing: The system of bracing used between floor or other timbers to distribute the weight. Bridging joist. Same as Binding joist.
brutalize: To make brutal; beasty; unfeeling; or inhuman. | To become brutal, inhuman, barbarous, or coarse and beasty. He mixed . . . with his countrymen, brutalized with them in their habits and manners. Addison.
brucine: A poweful vegetable alkaloid, found, associated with strychnine, in the seeds of different species of Strychnos, especially in the Nux vomica. It is less powerful than strychnine. Called also brucia and brucina.
brushite: A white or gray crystalline mineral consisting of the acid phosphate of calcium.
brucite: (a) A white, pearly mineral, occurring thin and foliated, like talc, and also fibrous; a native magnesium hydrate. (b) The mineral chondrodite.
brotherinlaw: The brother of one's husband or wife; also, the husband of one's sister; sometimes, the husband of one's wife's sister.
brethren: pl. of Brother. Note: This form of the plural is used, for the most part, in solemn address, and in speaking of religious sects or fraternities, or their members.
branchiopoda: An order of Entomostraca; -- so named from the feet of branchiopods having been supposed to perform the function of gills. It includes the fresh-water genera Branchipus, Apus, and Limnadia, and the genus Artemia found in salt lakes. It is also called Phyllopoda. See Phyllopoda, Cladocera. It is sometimes used in a broader sense.
broma: 1. (Med.) Aliment; food. Dunglison. 2. A light form of prepared cocoa (or cacao), or the drink made from it.
brashy: 1. Resembling, or of the nature of, brash, or broken fragments; broken; crumbly. Our progress was not at all impeded by the few soft, brashy floes that we encountered. F. T. Bullen. 2. Showery; characterized by brashes, or showers.
bromize: To prepare or treat with bromine; as, to bromize a silvered plate.
bridegroom: A man newly married, or just about to be married.
brachycephaly: The state or condition of being brachycephalic; shortness of head.
brigand: 1. A light-armed, irregular foot soldier. (old) 2. A lawless fellow who lives by plunder; one of a band of robbers; especially, one of a gang living in mountain retreats; a highwayman; a freebooter. Giving them not a little the air of brigands or banditti. Jeffery.
brockenspecter: A mountain specter (which see), esp. that observed on the Brocken, in the Harz Mountains.
bryony: The common name of several cucurbitaceous plants of the genus Bryonia. The root of B. alba (rough or white bryony) and of B. dioica is a strong, irritating cathartic. Black bryony, a plant (Tamus communis) so named from its dark glossy leaves and black root; black bindweed.
brownist: A follower of Robert Brown, of England, in the 16th century, who taught that every church is complete and independent in itself when organized, and consists of members meeting in one place, having… | One who advocates the Brunonian system of medicine.
brickyard: A place where bricks are made, especially an inclosed place.
broadax: 1. An ancient military weapon; a battle-ax. 2. An ax with a broad edge, for hewing timber.
brouded: Braided; broidered. (old) Alle his clothes brouded up and down. Chaucer.
bran: 1. The broken coat of the seed of wheat, rye, or other cereal grain, separated from the flour or meal by sifting or bolting; the coarse, chaffy part of ground grain. 2. (Zoöl.) The European carrion crow.
bridgepot: The adjustable socket, or step, of a millstone spindle. Knight.
broth: Liquid in which flesh (and sometimes other substances, as barley or rice) has been boiled; thin or simple soup. I am sure by your unprejudiced discourses that you love broth better than soup. Addison.
brahminism: The religion or system of doctrines of the Brahmans; the religion of Brahma.
brookite: A mineral consisting of titanic oxide, and hence identical with rutile and octahedrite in composition, but crystallizing in the orthorhombic system.
broche: Woven with a figure; as, broché goods.
brownness: The quality or state of being brown. Now like I brown (O lovely brown thy hair); Only in brownness beauty dwelleth there. Drayton.
broider: To embroider. (old) They shall make a broidered coat. Ex. xxviii. 4.
breasting: The curved channel in which a breast wheel turns. It is closely adapted to the curve of the wheel through about a quarter of its circumference, and prevents the escape of the water until it has spent its force upon the wheel. See Breast wheel.
bromatologist: One versed in the science of foods.
breech: 1. The lower part of the body behind; the buttocks. 2. Breeches. (old) Shak. 3. The hinder part of anything; esp., the part of a cannon, or other firearm, behind the chamber. 4. | 1. To put into, or clothe with, breeches. A great man . . . anxious to know whether the blacksmith's youngest boy was breeched. Macaulay. 2. To cover as with breeches.
bridler: One who bridles; one who restrains and governs, as with a bridle. Milton.
braying: Making a harsh noise; blaring. "Braying trumpets." Shak.
breathful: Full of breath; full of odor; fragrant. (old)
brachycephalous: Having the skull short in proportion to its breadth; shortheaded; -- in distinction from dolichocephalic.
bragly: In a manner to be bragged of; finely; proudly. (old) Spenser.
breakcircuit: A key or other device for breaking an electrical circuit.
branchpilot: A pilot who has a branch or commission, as from Trinity House, England, for special navigation.
broacher: 1. A spit; a broach. On five sharp broachers ranked, the roast they turned. Dryden. 2. One who broaches, opens, or utters; a first publisher or promoter. Some such broacher of heresy. Atterbury.
brighten: 1. To make bright or brighter; to make to shine; to increase the luster of; to give a brighter hue to. 2. To make illustrious, or more distinguished; to add luster or splendor to. | To grow bright, or more bright; to become less dark or gloomy; to clear up; to become bright or cheerful. And night shall brighten into day. N. Cotton. And, all his prospects brightening to the last,…
brightly: 1. Brilliantly; splendidly; with luster; as, brightly shining armor. 2. With lively intelligence; intelligently. Looking brightly into the mother's face. Hawthorne.
brambly: Pertaining to, resembling, or full of, brambles. "In brambly wildernesses." Tennyson.
brewing: 1. The act or process of preparing liquors which are brewed, as beer and ale. 2. The quantity brewed at once. A brewing of new beer, set by old beer. Bacon. 3. A mixing together. I am not able to avouch anything for certainty, such a brewing and sophistication of them they make. Holland. 4. (Naut.) A gathering or forming of a storm or squall, indicated by thick, dark clouds.
briefness: The quality of being brief; brevity; conciseness in discourse or writing.
brach: A bitch of the hound kind. Shak.
braise: A European marine fish (Pagrus vulgaris) allied to the American scup; the becker. The name is sometimes applied to the related species. [Also written brazier.] | 1. Charcoal powder; breeze. 2. (Cookery) Braised meat.
bristleshaped: Resembling a bristle in form; as, a bristle-shaped leaf.
brennage: A tribute which tenants paid to their lord, in lieu of bran, which they were obliged to furnish for his hounds.
brachypteres: A group of birds, including auks, divers, and penguins.
brownbill: A bill or halberd of the 16th and 17th centuries. See 4th Bill. Many time, but for a sallet, my brainpan had been cleft with a brown bill. Shak. Note: The black, or as it is sometimes called, the brown bill, was a kind of halberd, the cutting part hooked like a woodman's bill, from the back of which projected a spike, and another from the head. Grose.
brachial: 1. (Anat.) Pertaining or belonging to the arm; as, the brachial artery; the brachial nerve. 2. Of the nature of an arm; resembling an arm.
bravado: Boastful and threatening behavior; a boastful menace. In spite of our host's bravado. Irving.
branchial: Of or pertaining to branchiæ or gills. Branchial arches, the bony or cartilaginous arches which support the gills on each side of the throat of fishes and amphibians. See Illustration in Appendix. -- Branchial clefts, the openings between the branchial arches through which water passes.
brassiere: A form of woman's underwaist stiffened with whalebones, or the like, and worn to support the breasts.
bronchia: The bronchial tubes which arise from the branching of the trachea, esp. the subdivision of the bronchi. Dunglison.
brakeman: 1. (Railroads) A man in charge of a brake or brakes. 2. (Mining) The man in charge of the winding (or hoisting) engine for a mine.
branlin: A young salmon or parr, in the stage in which it has transverse black bands, as if burned by a gridiron. | A small red worm or larva, used as bait for small fresh-water fish; -- so called from its red color.
brassy: 1. Of or pertaining to brass; having the nature, appearance, or hardness, of brass. 2. Impudent; impudently bold. [Colloq.]
brickle: Brittle; easily broken. [Obs. or Prov.] Spenser. As stubborn steel excels the brickle glass. Turbervile.
bryonin: A bitter principle obtained from the root of the bryony (Bryonia alba and B. dioica). It is a white, or slightly colored, substance, and is emetic and cathartic.
brachiolaria: (Zoöl.) A peculiar early larval stage of certain starfishes, having a bilateral structure, and swimming by means of bands of vibrating cilia.
breloque: A seal or charm for a watch chain. "His chains and breloques." Thackeray.
brachyceral: Having short antennæ, as certain insects.
bromyrite: Silver bromide, a rare mineral; -- called also bromargyrite.
brodekin: A buskin or half-boot. [Written also brodequin.] (old)
brussels: A city of Belgium, giving its name to a kind of carpet, a kind of lace, etc. Brussels carpet, a kind of carpet made of worsted yarn fixed in a foundation web of strong linen thread. The worsted, which alone shows on the upper surface in drawn up in loops to form the pattern. -- Brussels ground, a name given to the handmade ground of real Brussels lace.
breechsight: A device attached to the breech of a firearm, to guide the eye, in conjunction with the front sight, in taking aim.
bravo: A daring villain; a bandit; one who sets law at defiance; a professional assassin or murderer. Safe from detection, seize the unwary prey. And stab, like bravoes, all who come this way. Churchill. | Well done! excellent! an exclamation expressive of applause.
brachygrapher: A writer in short hand; a stenographer. He asked the brachygrapher whether he wrote the notes of the sermon. Gayton.
bryozoan: Of or pertaining to the Bryozoa. -- n. One of the Bryozoa.
brow: 1. The prominent ridge over the eye, with the hair that covers it, forming an arch above the orbit. And his arched brow, pulled o'er his eyes, With solemn proof proclaims him wise. Churchill. 2. | To bound to limit; to be at, or form, the edge of. Tending my flocks hard by i' the hilly crofts That brow this bottom glade. Milton.
bride: 1. A woman newly married, or about to be married. Has by his own experience tried How much the wife is dearer than the bride. Lyttleton. I will show thee the bride, the Lamb's wife. Rev. xxi. 9. 2. Fig.: An object ardently loved. Bride of the sea, the city of Venice.
brachyptera: A group of Coleoptera having short wings; the rove beetles.
bruteness: 1. Brutality. (old) Spenser. 2. Insensibility. "The bruteness of nature." Emerson.
brutify: To make like a brute; to make senseless, stupid, or unfeeling; to brutalize. Any man not quite brutified and void of sense. Barrow.
bromlife: A carbonate of baryta and lime, intermediate between witherite and strontianite; -- called also alstonite.
briar: 1. A plant with a slender woody stem bearing stout prickles; especially, species of Rosa, Rubus, and Smilax. 2. Fig.: Anything sharp or unpleasant to the feelings. The thorns and briers of reproof. Cowper. Brier root, the root of the southern Smilax laurifolia and S. Walleri; -- used for tobacco pipes. -- Cat brier, Green brier, several species of Smilax (S.
brace: 1. That which holds anything tightly or supports it firmly; a bandage or a prop. 2. A cord, ligament, or rod, for producing or maintaining tension, as a cord on the side of a drum. | 1. To furnish with braces; to support; to prop; as, to brace a beam in a building. 2. To draw tight; to tighten; to put in a state of tension; to strain; to strengthen; as, to brace the nerves.
branch: 1. (Bot.) A shoot or secondary stem growing from the main stem, or from a principal limb or bough of a tree or other plant. 2. Any division extending like a branch; | Diverging from, or tributary to, a main stock, line, way, theme, etc.; as, a branch vein; a branch road or line; a branch topic; a branch store.
breton: Of or relating to Brittany, or Bretagne, in France. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Brittany, or Bretagne, in France; also, the ancient language of Brittany; Armorican.
